claim: Uniform national swing works historically not because swing is literally identical in every constituency but because deviations from the average swing tend to cancel out symmetrically across seats; when that symmetry breaks, UNS becomes actively misleading rather than merely imprecise.
stance_target: uniform swing's historical accuracy validates its underlying literal assumption
quoted_support: The real statistical assumption underlying uniform swing, then, is not the obviously absurd notion that the swing in each seat is identical, but that deviations from the average are symmetrical.

claim: Ahead of the UK 2015 election, Scotland diverged sharply and asymmetrically from England/Wales -- SNP led Labour by 16 points in a late-2014 poll versus Labour's 22-point lead over the SNP in 2010 -- and modeling Scotland separately from a single GB-wide uniform swing reduced Labour's projected seat total by about 20 net seats (11 extra English/Welsh gains swamped by 31 Scottish losses).
stance_target: a single nationwide uniform swing correctly captures regionally divergent partisan realignment
quoted_support: Labour's 11 extra gains south of the border are swamped by its 31 losses north of the border. The overall effect is to reduce Labour's GB-wide total by 20 seats.

claim: A well-documented incumbency/sophomore-surge effect worth roughly 2 percentage points of vote share for first-term MPs seeking re-election means marginal seats held by incumbents see below-average swing against them, which can save an incumbent party around 20 seats it would otherwise lose under a plain uniform-swing projection.
stance_target: uniform swing correctly treats incumbent-held marginal seats the same as open seats
scope_conditions: United Kingdom, first-term MPs, three decades of historical pattern
quoted_support: For the past three decades, there has been a consistent trend for new MPs to do slightly better than the average, the first time they seek re-election. On average, the bonus is worth 2%... this would allow the Tories to hold on to around 20 seats they would otherwise lose.
